newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION - Auckland, Natal the teams to beat-Mordt.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - Auckland, Natal the teams to beat-Mordt.

text.p: AUCKLAND, April 16 - Gauteng Lions coach Ray Mordt picks last year's Super 12 rugby finalists the Auckland Blues and the Natal Sharks as the sides to beat in this year's competition, NZPA reports.
Mordt's team, previously known as Transvaal, play the Blues in their first away assignment of the season -- at Eden Park on Saturday -- and he spoke of the stern task ahead.

"We possibly would have preferred to have played Auckland later in this tour, but the thing is we have to play them first so maybe it will be good to get this one over with," Mordt said shortly after arriving in Auckland yesterday.
He backed ACT Brumbies coach Rod Macqueen's comment that Auckland were the benchmark side in the competition this year.
"Auckland are the team, and Natal are also a great team, so when they play it will be an awesome game," the former Springbok back, who inherited the job from ex-All Blacks coach Alex Wyllie, said.
"Auckland have the game plan and the players to execute it for them.
"They can play it expansively or keep it tight, they're capable of producing any type of game they want.
"They have the players and the skills which makes the difference between them and the other teams in the tournament."
As a competitor Mordt always remained unbowed, even if bloodied in defeat, and his fighting words were no different on arrival.
"We also have some very good players in our team and have no doubt about it they won't be shirking," he said.
"I'm pretty confident my side is going to come out charged up. We'll be there putting in a good show and that is what it is all about."
Mordt said Transvaal's success this year was the result of a turnaround in personnel and the unity that has since developed in the squad.
"Our preparations this year have been different. At the beginning of the season we had a few internal problems," he said.
"But all of that has been put behind us and we've also benefited from playing our early games at home.
"But now we're down to the tough side of the tournament, everyone has to do it, everyone has to play it and we're looking forward to it."
Like every coach visiting another country, Mordt also repeated a plea for consistency in refereeing.
"Games for teams away and home are getting close, what we want is to get the interpretations of the laws right," he said.
Mordt added his voice to the growing chorus of calls for a neutral panel of referees for the tournament.
Auckland trained last night and bracketed injured fullback Adrian Cashmore with his predecessor Shane Howarth who has been called into the squad as a temporary replacement.
Otherwise, Auckland have named the same side which beat the ACT Brumbies 41-29 last weekend.
Gauteng Lions hope to name their team after training today.

Auckland Blues: Adrian Cashmore or Shane Howarth, Joeli Vidiri, Eroni Clarke, Brian Lima, Lee Stensness, Carlos Spencer, Ofisa Tonu'u, Zinzan Brooke (captain), Mark Carter, Leo Lafaiali'i, Jim Coe, Michael Jones, Craig Dowd, Sean Fitzpatrick, Paul Thomson. Reserves to be named later.
